Detect unused code in .NET solutions

Usage:
  dotnet-unused [path] [options]

Arguments:
  path               Path to .sln, .slnx, or .csproj file

Options:
  --format, -f       Output format: text, json, or markdown (default: text)
  --output, -o       Output file path (for JSON or markdown format)
  --exclude-public   Exclude public members (default: true)
  --skip-usings      Skip unused using directives analysis (default: false)
  --fix              Automatically remove unused usings (default: false)
  --unused-packages  Detect unused NuGet packages (default: false)
  --fail-on-unused  Exit with code 2 when any unused code is found (for CI 
gating; default: exit 0)
  --strict          Treat project load errors as fatal instead of analyzing a 
partially loaded solution (default: false)
  --include-virtual  Also report unused virtual members (default: false; 
virtuals are skipped because polymorphism can hide their uses)
  --ignore-attributes  Never flag members with these attributes 
(comma-separated)
  --exclude-packages  Never flag these NuGet packages as unused 
(comma-separated; requires --unused-packages)
  --verbose, -v      Explain why each NuGet package was judged used, unused, or 
skipped (requires --unused-packages)
  --msbuild-path     Directory of the MSBuild to use, e.g. a .NET SDK folder (or
set DOTNET_UNUSED_MSBUILD_PATH)
  --help, -h         Show help information

Examples:
  dotnet-unused MySolution.sln
  dotnet-unused MyProject.csproj --format json --
